content:
The evolutionary explanation has not been tested here
A description of egalitarian social practices does not establish the ancestral selection history of a modern reader’s embarrassment about achievement. Several mechanisms could produce the same feeling. The text provides no evidence that discriminates its adaptation story from those alternatives.

quote: ashamed of wanting to do better than others
content:
Equal moral standing does not require equal performance
One can affirm equal rights while recognizing large differences in skill. Likewise, wanting to improve does not require ranking other people’s worth beneath one’s own. The useful case for excellence survives without making egalitarian ethics the obstacle.

quote: who are below average? Do you
content:
The average is not an upper bound
Surpassing the current average can be a worthwhile aspiration, and compulsory self-deprecation can obstruct honest assessment. The task still needs an absolute performance target and feedback. Relative rank may rise because others decline; it is an unreliable substitute for becoming more capable.
